parsed.title: Fixture ledger rows contradict the fixture's own stub files
parsed.detail: The dogfood ledger cites `scripts/phase-lint.mjs:293-305`, `SPEC.md:95,405-419`, `PLAN.md:27`, `ACCEPTANCE.md (AC8)`, `docs/LOGS.md:1`, etc., but the fixture's actual files are one-line stubs (`# SPEC stub (fixture)`, `// stub cited by the dogfood ledger rows`). The router parses these rows for read-set/cited paths; the cited line numbers and paths cannot exist in the fixture, so any test asserting the router resolves these citations is testing against fabricated evidence.

parsed.title: F89 cites docs/LOGS.md:1 but the fixture LOGS.md is a different file
parsed.detail: F89 says `docs/LOGS.md:1` should be relocated below the `# Session log` H1 + intro block, but the fixture's `docs/LOGS.md` is a single line `# Session log stub (cited by a FOLDED row only)` with no H1/intro/entry. The finding's evidence does not match the fixture it lives in.

parsed.title: F92 cites PLAN.md:93 and 38-PLAN/TASKS line numbers that don't exist in the stubs
parsed.detail: F92 references `docs/features/37-phase-lint-script/PLAN.md:93` and `38-.../{PLAN.md:29,TASKS.md:55}`, but the fixture's 38 PLAN/TASKS are one-line stubs (`# PLAN stub for unit 38`, `# TASKS stub for unit 38`) and 37 has no PLAN.md at all in this slice. The cited line numbers are impossible.

parsed.title: Cited-paths fixture cites src/file-7..9 and 14..15 but those files exist and are not in the read-set
parsed.detail: F1's route text says 'cites src/file-7.txt and src/file-8.txt and src/file-9.txt' and F2 cites file-14/15; all of those files exist in the fixture. If the router's read-set is derived from the `file:line` column only, the route prose citations are not exercised; if it also scans route prose, the fixture's 'cap case' (20 files) is not actually capped at the intended boundary. Either way the fixture does not demonstrate the cap behavior its name claims.

parsed.title: F3 route has no citations but F1/F2 do — cap-case asymmetry undocumented
parsed.detail: F1 and F2 route text appends 'cites src/file-N.txt ...' while F3's route is bare 'replan-in-unit: plan owner re-cuts'. If the router's cited-path extraction is meant to be tested, the asymmetry between rows is unexplained and the fixture does not state which behavior is expected.

parsed.title: Roadmap lists 37 as `idea` but the fixture ships a full review-findings ledger for it
parsed.detail: ROADMAP.md row `| 37 | phase-lint-script | idea | — | dogfood target |` declares unit 37 as `idea`, yet the fixture contains `docs/features/37-phase-lint-script/{SPEC,ACCEPTANCE,review-findings}.md` with a 21-line ledger. A unit at `idea` status should not have a review-findings ledger; the router's status-vs-ledger consistency check (if any) is contradicted by the fixture.

parsed.title: Unit 14 `empty-unit` is `planned` but has no SPEC/ACCEPTANCE
parsed.detail: ROADMAP row `| 14 | empty-unit | planned | — | no ledger |` and the folder contains only `.gitkeep`. If the router treats `planned` units as requiring SPEC.md (per the repo's own unit contract), the fixture encodes an invalid state; if `planned` legitimately has no SPEC, the fixture should say so. The 'no ledger' summary is the only hint.

parsed.title: Fix README row `pending` status has no matching unit folder and no declared vocabulary
parsed.detail: `| [#20](...) | pending-topic | `pending` | tracked issue, no unit folder |` — the status `pending` is not one of the statuses used elsewhere in this material (`in-progress`, `planned`, `idea`). If the router validates fix statuses against a closed enum, this fixture row is out-of-enum; if not, the fixture is silently exercising an undocumented status.

parsed.title: F2 route text `replan-in-unit: plan owner re-cuts the phase` has no cited path
parsed.detail: F2 is `high` severity with class `fix-now` but route `replan-in-unit: ...` — the class/route pairing contradicts the fixture's own F1 (`fix-now` → `fold into phase`) and F3 (`decision-required` → `surface decision, block`). A `fix-now` finding routed to `replan-in-unit` is not one of the declared class→route mappings visible in this material.

parsed.title: Decision-unit F1 is `high` + `decision-required` but 10-replan-unit F3 is `med` + `decision-required`
parsed.detail: The two fixtures disagree on whether `decision-required` implies a severity floor. If the router's route selection is severity-driven, the fixtures do not pin the expected behavior; if class-driven, the severity difference is irrelevant but undocumented.

parsed.title: `folded: yes` row still has route `fold into phase` — folded rows should be terminal
parsed.detail: F1 in 13-execute-unit is `folded: yes` but its route column still reads `fold into phase`. A folded finding has already been folded; the route should be terminal (e.g. `n/a` or `folded`). The router's 'all folded' summary for unit 13 depends on this row being recognized as folded, but the route text contradicts the folded flag.
